S.closing:
A year on, nobody at Lindenmarkt calls it "the Shelfcast project" any more.
They just call it the forecast, and they plan around it.
S.spiral_closing: This cycle closes with Shelfcast trusted enough that the next argument is about what else it should decide, not whether it should decide anything.

scoreboard.availability: Shoppers find the article on the shelf, including in the middle aisle week.
scoreboard.waste: Fresh waste is down to what the category team considers normal loss.
scoreboard.residual_stock: Promotion weeks end close to clean. The warehouse is not holding last season's garden furniture.
scoreboard.override_rate: Store managers rarely override the suggestion now. When they do, the team goes and looks, because it usually means something real.

A.closing:
Shelfcast runs the nightly forecast for every store, and the buyers have stopped keeping a private spreadsheet next to it.
That second part took longer than the first.
A.spiral_closing: This cycle ends with the platform doing its job and the room mostly agreeing on what it should do next.

scoreboard.availability: Availability is better than the year before, clearly enough that the regions noticed.
scoreboard.waste: Fresh waste is down, though nobody would call it solved.
scoreboard.residual_stock: Most promotion weeks land near their allocation. The misses are smaller than they used to be.
scoreboard.override_rate: Overrides have fallen. A few regions still run their own way and nobody has pushed the issue.

B.closing:
Shelfcast is live and it is genuinely better than the spreadsheets, which is not the same as the project having gone well.
The team knows the difference.
B.spiral_closing: This cycle leaves a working platform with a list of things everyone agrees should have been done differently.

scoreboard.availability: Availability improved on the core range. The middle aisle is still a lottery.
scoreboard.waste: Waste moved a little. The weather feed helps on the days it is right.
scoreboard.residual_stock: Promotion residuals are roughly where they were, which the buyers point out regularly.
scoreboard.override_rate: Overrides are down in the regions that were consulted and flat in the ones that were not.

C.closing:
Shelfcast forecasts every night and the stores work around it.
The platform is real; the trust that was supposed to come with it is not, yet.
C.spiral_closing: This cycle ends with the platform running and the room no more convinced than when it started.

scoreboard.availability: Availability is about where it was. The cases everyone complained about still happen.
scoreboard.waste: Fresh waste is unchanged. Nobody can agree whether that is the model or the ordering rules.
scoreboard.residual_stock: Residual stock after a promotion week is still a buyer's problem, solved by instinct.
scoreboard.override_rate: Store managers override roughly as often as before, and now they have a year of examples.

D.closing:
Shelfcast runs, after a fashion.
Twice this quarter the forecast missed the morning order window and the stores ordered blind, and everyone remembers both days.
D.spiral_closing: This cycle ends with more to undo than to build on, and the room knows it.

scoreboard.availability: Availability is worse in the regions that leaned on the suggestions. They have stopped leaning.
scoreboard.waste: Waste is up on fresh, and the weekly review has started opening with it.
scoreboard.residual_stock: There are pallets of an advertised promotion still in the warehouse, six weeks after the week ended.
scoreboard.override_rate: The override rate is higher than before the project started. That number is the one management asks about.

E.closing:
Nobody cancels Shelfcast.
It keeps running, and the stores keep ignoring it, and the buyers keep their spreadsheets open beside it. A year, spent to arrive back where it began, with the added knowledge that this was the attempt.
E.spiral_closing: This cycle ends with the platform trusted less than when it started, which is the one outcome the team was told to avoid.

scoreboard.availability: Availability is no better, and in the promotion weeks it is worse.
scoreboard.waste: Fresh waste is up. The category team has gone back to ordering the way they did before.
scoreboard.residual_stock: An advertised article sold out on the first morning in half the estate. A different one is still on pallets.
scoreboard.override_rate: Almost every suggested order is overridden. The signal the model needs is gone, because nobody is following it.

beats.text: {st}'s trust never recovered. By the end they had stopped raising objections in meetings entirely, not because they agreed but because raising them had stopped changing anything.
A concern {st} raised and was overruled on came back later as a real incident, one that took a week to fix.
{stage} broke and was never repaired. Every stage downstream of it has been working with whatever degraded output it produces.
The team misread what stakeholders actually needed more often than not, mistaking hard boundaries for mere preferences, so proposals kept hitting the same objections.
The team consistently understood what each stakeholder actually needed before proposing anything, which is why objections stayed rare.
More than one proposal was rejected outright. After that the team played it safe, and nobody proposed the bigger fix again.
Nothing shipped over anyone's objections. Every change that went through had the backing of the person it affected.
Relations across the room stayed strong throughout. Whoever runs the next cycle inherits people who will raise problems early.
The team shipped what it could agree on, and left the rest for the next cycle. Most projects end this way; few admit it.
